public_rationale: Contemporary research supports Marcus's point that opacity makes debugging harder. But the stronger explanation overstates the limits of existing methods: before the post, ROME demonstrated causal investigation of factual recall and targeted edits to model weights. The difficulty claim holds in this narrower sense; the assertion that useful understanding and targeted remedies were absent does not.
limitations: The evidence concerns neural language models, not every deep learning application.
The supporting survey gives a qualitative assessment, not a controlled estimate of the causal contribution of opacity.
The mixed verdict depends on treating the assertion about absent remedies as a substantive commitment rather than loose rhetoric.

our_interpretation: Assess the state of knowledge available when the post appeared, on 2022-05-31. The target period has no lower bound because established earlier methods remain relevant to that state.
The ordinary reading is that limited understanding makes diagnosis and repair difficult, and that practitioners lack effective targeted remedies beyond broadly changing data, training, or model size.
Assess the difficulty and its proposed explanation separately. A targeted repair need not solve debugging generally to count against the assertion that such remedies were unknown.
Do not interpret 'understands' as requiring complete mathematical understanding, or 'and so forth' as automatically encompassing every possible repair.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous research or engineering evidence shows that model opacity materially obstructed diagnosis and repair, and that effective remedies were generally limited to broad data or training changes.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous work demonstrates useful understanding of internal mechanisms and effective targeted repairs beyond collecting more data or enlarging models. Evidence that debugging was routinely straightforward would also contradict the difficulty claim.
